_instructions: This is THE SINGLE FILE you fill in once to configure the entire pipeline.
Every script reads from this file — auto_prep.py, validate_prep.py, generate_summaries.py, generate_covers.py.
Fill every field marked YOUR_... then run: python3 scripts/check_workflow.py
Fields with '_doc' keys are documentation only — they are NOT read by any script.
Tip: start with 'contact', 'education', 'experience', and 'core_skills' — those affect every output.

contact._doc: Appears in resume header and cover letter closing. Use your professional details.
contact.name: YOUR FULL NAME
contact.eor_address: Your Country | Remote (EOR-ready: Deel / Remote.com) | UTC+X aligned

visa_addresses._doc: Address line suffix per market for visa-required applications. Remove markets you don't target. If you already have right to work in a market, add it to has_right_to_work.markets instead — that skips the visa framing entirely for those markets.
visa_addresses.uk: Your Country | Seeking Skilled Worker Visa Sponsorship
visa_addresses.de: Your Country | Seeking EU Blue Card Sponsorship
visa_addresses.dk: Your Country | Seeking Pay Limit Scheme Sponsorship
visa_addresses.ie: Your Country | Seeking Critical Skills Employment Permit
visa_addresses.ae: Your Country | Seeking UAE Employment Visa Sponsorship

has_right_to_work._doc: Markets where you ALREADY have work authorization — no visa sponsorship needed. Use market codes: uk, nl, de, dk, ie, se, ae. Leave [] if you need sponsorship everywhere. EXAMPLES: EU citizen targeting EU markets → add 'nl', 'de', 'ie'. UK ILR holder → add 'uk'. Australian citizen targeting AU → not applicable (no AU market in this pipeline).

education._doc: Most recent first. Remove the 'gpa' key entirely if you don't want GPA on your resume.

experience._doc: Reverse chronological order (newest first). bank_key MUST EXACTLY match a ## heading in experience_bank.md. max_bullets controls how many bullets auto_prep.py selects per role. focus_areas guides bullet prioritisation — put keywords matching the role's core work.
experience.bank_key: Exact heading text from experience_bank.md (e.g. 'Company Name')
experience.focus_areas: keyword1 · keyword2 · keyword3 — drives bullet selection priority

core_skills._doc: Always in Skills section of resume — every application. List your top technical tools, priority order. These appear FIRST in the Skills section before any JD-conditional skills. EXAMPLES (analytics): ['SQL', 'Python', 'Tableau', 'BigQuery']. EXAMPLES (software eng): ['Python', 'Go', 'Kubernetes', 'AWS', 'PostgreSQL']. EXAMPLES (finance): ['Excel', 'Python', 'SQL', 'Bloomberg', 'VBA'].

domains._doc: Define work domains relevant to YOUR profession. The pipeline detects which domain a JD belongs to from its text, then selects matching bullets and expertise labels from experience_bank.md. Add/remove domain keys freely — each must also appear in headline_by_domain below. The 'general' domain is the catch-all fallback and should always exist.

primary._doc: Your main domain — highest bullet selection priority when detected. EXAMPLE (analytics): label='Product Analytics', keywords=['product analytics', 'growth', 'experimentation', 'a/b test']. EXAMPLE (software eng): label='Backend Engineering', keywords=['microservices', 'api', 'distributed systems', 'backend']. EXAMPLE (finance): label='FP&A', keywords=['financial planning', 'budgeting', 'forecasting', 'fp&a'].
primary.label: Your Primary Domain Label (e.g. 'Product Analytics', 'Backend Engineering', 'FP&A')

secondary._doc: Second most common domain in your target JDs. Follows same pattern as primary.
secondary.label: Your Secondary Domain Label

general._doc: Catch-all when no specific domain is detected. Use your broadest professional credentials.
general.label: General / Strategy

expertise._doc: Core Expertise section of the resume. 3 primary specialisms + 2-3 secondary shown per role. 'pinned' items always appear regardless of domain. 'leadership' items added when JD is manager/lead level. EXAMPLES (analytics): primary=['Product Analytics', 'Experimentation & A/B Testing', 'CRM Analytics']. EXAMPLES (software): primary=['Distributed Systems', 'Platform Engineering', 'API Design']. EXAMPLES (finance): primary=['Financial Modelling', 'FP&A', 'Commercial Strategy'].

headline_by_domain._doc: Resume headline shown directly under your name. One entry per domain key (must match domain keys above). 'default' = IC/specialist roles. 'leadership' = Manager/Lead/Head roles. First array element is the title; second is the subtitle tagline. EXAMPLE: {"primary": {"default": ["Lead Analytics Professional", "Product · Growth · Experimentation"], "leadership": ["Analytics Lead & Manager", "Product · Growth · AI"]}}.

leadership: YOUR LEADERSHIP TITLE FOR PRIMARY DOMAIN
YOUR LEADERSHIP TITLE FOR SECONDARY DOMAIN

resume_tags._doc: Tags used to label bullets in experience_bank.md. Each bullet can carry one or more [tag] markers; the pipeline uses these for domain-matched bullet selection. Must match what you use in experience_bank.md. EXAMPLES (analytics): ['product', 'growth', 'crm', 'pricing', 'experimentation', 'ai', 'leadership', 'bi']. EXAMPLES (software): ['backend', 'infrastructure', 'api', 'performance', 'security', 'leadership']. EXAMPLES (finance): ['fp_and_a', 'modelling', 'reporting', 'commercial', 'risk', 'leadership'].

profile._doc: Used in Pass 2 scoring prompt, validation checks, and profile summary generation.

industry_history._doc: Industries you have ACTUALLY worked in — used in Profile Summary S1 framing. 2-3 industries max. Be honest — the validation suite checks this. EXAMPLES (analytics): ['ecommerce', 'marketplace', 'agri-tech']. EXAMPLES (software): ['fintech', 'SaaS', 'infrastructure']. EXAMPLES (finance): ['investment banking', 'asset management', 'corporate finance'].

verbatim_sentences._doc: Sentences appended verbatim to the end of every Profile Summary after the LLM-generated sentences. Use for credentials you always want highlighted. Leave 'sentences' as [] to disable. 'investment_sentence' is appended only for finance/investment-domain JDs if non-empty. EXAMPLE sentence: 'Brings current hands-on AI automation experience, having built a production agentic pipeline using [YOUR_TOOL].'

platform_notes._doc: Per-employer data platform rules — prevents credibility-risk tool mix-ups in cover letters. Format: {"Company Name": "description of platform used"}. EXAMPLE: {"Acme Corp": "used AWS Redshift — never say BigQuery for this role", "StartupX": "used GCP BigQuery — never say Redshift"}. Leave {} if not needed.

framing_rules._doc: Special framing instructions for specific employers or career stints. Applied to cover letter and summary generation. Array of plain-English rules. EXAMPLE: ["Always describe the Singapore stint as '2 years onsite in Singapore during a 5-year tenure' — never as a separate company."]. Leave [] if not needed.

required_portfolio_tools._doc: V1 validation check: tools you've built public/portfolio work with. When a JD mentions these tools, they are validated to appear in your cover letter. Leave [] to skip this check.

excluded_tools._doc: V2 validation check: tools you've used historically but cannot confidently defend in interviews. Blocked from Skills section, Core Expertise, Profile Summary, and Cover Letter paragraphs. They CAN still appear in work_history bullets (factual historical record). Leave [] to skip. EXAMPLE: ['Google Analytics', 'Firebase', 'Apache Airflow'] — tools used but not interview-ready.

canonical_metrics._doc: V7 validation check: exact metric strings that must appear unchanged in every resume output. Prevents the LLM from paraphrasing your real numbers into approximate language. Leave [] to skip. EXAMPLE: ['40%', '30%', '85%'] — these exact strings must appear verbatim, never as 'approximately 40%' or 'around a third'.

industry_whitelist._doc: V17 validation check: industries you can honestly claim in cover letters. Leave [] to allow any industry reference. EXAMPLE: ['ecommerce', 'marketplace', 'agri-tech', 'automotive'] — cover letter will only reference these, never claim fintech/SaaS/etc. experience you don't have.
